symbols.name: first map
symbols.meaning: A linear map on vectors of length $s$.
symbols.quote: Let $L$ be a linear map on vectors of length $s$ and $M$ a linear map on vectors of length $t$, with entries $L_{ih}$ (row $i$, column $h$) and $M_{mg}$ (row $m$, column $g$).

symbols.name: second map
symbols.meaning: A linear map on vectors of length $t$.
symbols.quote: Let $L$ be a linear map on vectors of length $s$ and $M$ a linear map on vectors of length $t$, with entries $L_{ih}$ (row $i$, column $h$) and $M_{mg}$ (row $m$, column $g$).

symbols.name: tensor product
symbols.meaning: The operator that combines $L$ and $M$ into a linear map on arrays with $s$ rows and $t$ columns.
symbols.quote: The tensor product $L\otimes M$ is the linear map on arrays $u$ with $s$ rows and $t$ columns, entries $u_{hg}$, whose entry at position $(i,m)$ is

symbols.name: array
symbols.meaning: An array with $s$ rows and $t$ columns, whose entries are $u_{hg}$.
symbols.quote: The tensor product $L\otimes M$ is the linear map on arrays $u$ with $s$ rows and $t$ columns, entries $u_{hg}$, whose entry at position $(i,m)$ is

symbols.name: output row index
symbols.meaning: The index of an output row, which is the first coordinate of an output position.
symbols.quote: Here $i$ and $m$ index the output row and column, and $h$ and $g$ index the input row and column.

symbols.name: output column index
symbols.meaning: The index of an output column, which is the second coordinate of an output position.
symbols.quote: Here $i$ and $m$ index the output row and column, and $h$ and $g$ index the input row and column.

symbols.name: input row index
symbols.meaning: The index of an input row of the array $u$.
symbols.quote: Here $i$ and $m$ index the output row and column, and $h$ and $g$ index the input row and column.

symbols.name: input column index
symbols.meaning: The index of an input column of the array $u$.
symbols.quote: Here $i$ and $m$ index the output row and column, and $h$ and $g$ index the input row and column.

relations.quote: A tensor product is built from one [Linear map](linear-map.md) for each coordinate, and it lets a map on a multidimensional array act on each coordinate in turn.
